bank.name: History
bank.subject: Pakistan Affairs
bank.description: Key events of the Pakistan Movement and the history of Pakistan, from the Aligarh movement to the present.

questions.prompt: When was the Pakistan Resolution adopted?
questions.explanation: The Lahore Resolution (later renamed Pakistan Resolution) was adopted on 23 March 1940 at Minto Park, Lahore.

questions.prompt: Who moved the Pakistan Resolution at the Lahore session of the Muslim League in 1940?
questions.explanation: A. K. Fazlul Huq, the Prime Minister of Bengal, formally moved the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution.

questions.prompt: Who coined the name 'Pakistan'?
questions.explanation: Choudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name 'Pakistan' in his 1933 pamphlet 'Now or Never'.

questions.prompt: In which address did Allama Iqbal present the idea of a separate Muslim state in the subcontinent?
questions.explanation: Allama Iqbal delivered his famous Allahabad Address in 1930, proposing a separate homeland for the Muslims of the subcontinent.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah became the first Governor-General of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan (1947-1951).

questions.prompt: When was the Objectives Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution, which laid the foundation of the constitution, was passed on 12 March 1949.

questions.prompt: When was the first Constitution of Pakistan promulgated?
questions.explanation: The first Constitution of Pakistan was promulgated on 23 March 1956.

questions.prompt: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan when the 1956 Constitution came into effect; he was deposed in the 1958 martial law.

questions.prompt: When was the first martial law imposed in Pakistan, and by whom?
questions.explanation: General Ayub Khan imposed the first martial law on 7 October 1958.

questions.prompt: Which Constitution made Pakistan a parliamentary federal republic with a Prime Minister as head of government?
questions.explanation: The 1973 Constitution, promulgated on 14 August 1973 under Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, established the parliamentary system.

questions.prompt: When was the Tashkent Declaration signed after the 1965 Indo-Pakistan war?
questions.explanation: The Tashkent Declaration was signed in January 1966 between Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri, with Soviet mediation.

questions.prompt: Between whom was the Simla Agreement of 1972 signed?
questions.explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972, after the 1971 war.

questions.prompt: In which year did East Pakistan separate and become Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: East Pakistan separated on 16 December 1971, when Pakistan's forces surrendered in Dhaka.

questions.prompt: When did the 1973 Constitution come into effect?
questions.explanation: The 1973 Constitution was enforced on 14 August 1973.

questions.prompt: In which year and city was the All-India Muslim League founded?
questions.explanation: The All-India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at a meeting in Dhaka.

questions.prompt: Which British commission of 1928, with no Indian member, was boycotted by Indian parties?
questions.explanation: The all-white Simon Commission (1928) was boycotted across India with the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.

questions.prompt: When did Quaid-e-Azam present his famous Fourteen Points?
questions.explanation: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in 1929 in response to the Nehru Report.

questions.prompt: The boundary line drawn between India and Pakistan at partition in 1947 is named after which person?
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe to demarcate the India-Pakistan border in August 1947.

questions.prompt: In which year was the 'One Unit' scheme merging the provinces of West Pakistan introduced?
questions.explanation: The One Unit scheme was introduced in 1955 and remained in force until it was dissolved in 1970.

questions.prompt: When did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests at Chagai?
questions.explanation: Pakistan carried out five nuclear tests on 28 May 1998 at Chagai, Balochistan, followed by a sixth on 30 May.

questions.prompt: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was signed between which two leaders?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and Indian PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee signed the Lahore Declaration in February 1999.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman prime minister of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Benazir Bhutto became the first woman prime minister of Pakistan in 1988.

questions.prompt: The 1962 Constitution introduced which system of government?
options: A presidential system with an indirectly elected president
questions.explanation: Ayub Khan's 1962 Constitution established a strong presidential system.

questions.prompt: Who was the Chief Martial Law Administrator who imposed the second martial law in 1969?
questions.explanation: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law in March 1969.

questions.prompt: The 1970 general elections were won by which party in East Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's Awami League won a majority of seats in 1970, mostly in East Pakistan.

questions.prompt: When was the 1973 Constitution adopted by the National Assembly?
questions.explanation: The National Assembly unanimously approved the 1973 Constitution on 10 April 1973.

questions.prompt: Pakistan became the world's how many-th nuclear power in 1998?
questions.explanation: After the 1998 Chagai tests, Pakistan became the seventh nuclear weapons state.

questions.prompt: Who became the first President of Pakistan to be elected directly by the people?
questions.explanation: Musharraf won the 2002 referendum and 2004 presidential vote; Ayub Khan also used a referendum in 1960 and was elected by the Electoral College in 1965.

questions.prompt: The name 'Pakistan' was first used in which publication?
questions.explanation: Choudhry Rahmat Ali coined 'Pakistan' in the 1933 pamphlet 'Now or Never'.

questions.prompt: The 'Kamal Ataturk' reforms influenced which Pakistani leader?
questions.explanation: Jinnah admired Ataturk's modernization, which influenced his vision for Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Who was the last Governor-General of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Iskander Mirza was the last Governor-General before becoming the first President in 1956.

questions.prompt: Which Governor-General dismissed the first Constituent Assembly in 1954?
questions.explanation: Ghulam Muhammad dismissed the first Constituent Assembly in 1954.

questions.prompt: The 'Objective Resolution' was moved in the Constituent Assembly by?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan moved the Objectives Resolution on 7 March 1949.

questions.prompt: The 'Ayub Khan era' is often called?
questions.explanation: Ayub's 1960s rule promoted rapid industrialization and is called the Decade of Development.

questions.prompt: Which party won the 1970 general elections in West Pakistan?
questions.explanation: PPP led by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto won the majority of West Pakistan seats in 1970.

questions.prompt: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto served as which of the following first?
questions.explanation: Bhutto was Foreign Minister (1963-66), then President (1971-73), then PM (1973-77).

questions.prompt: The 1973 Constitution was drafted under whose leadership?
questions.explanation: Bhutto's government and the 1972 constitutional committee drafted the 1973 Constitution.

questions.prompt: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law in which year?
questions.explanation: Zia imposed martial law on 5 July 1977, overthrowing Bhutto.

questions.prompt: Zia-ul-Haq held the 'Islamization' and held a referendum in which year?
questions.explanation: Zia's 1984 referendum endorsed his Islamization agenda and presidency.

questions.prompt: Who became the first directly elected Prime Minister in 1985?
questions.explanation: Junejo was elected PM in the 1985 non-party elections under Zia.

questions.prompt: Benazir Bhutto became PM for the first time in which year?
questions.explanation: Benazir Bhutto became PM in December 1988 after Zia's death.

questions.prompt: The 'Kalabagh Dam' controversy primarily involves?
questions.explanation: The proposed Kalabagh Dam has faced provincial opposition over water shares.

questions.prompt: Who signed the 'Lahore Declaration' in 1999?
options: Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee
questions.explanation: Sharif and Vajpayee signed the Lahore Declaration in February 1999.

questions.prompt: The 'Kargil Conflict' of 1999 took place in which region?
questions.explanation: The Kargil conflict occurred along the Line of Control in Kashmir in 1999.

questions.prompt: General Pervez Musharraf took power in which year?
questions.explanation: Musharraf led the October 1999 coup against Nawaz Sharif.

questions.prompt: The 18th Amendment was passed under which PM?
questions.explanation: The 18th Amendment was passed in 2010 during Gilani's premiership.

questions.prompt: Which general election is known for the 'Terrorism and extremism' security backdrop of 2018?
questions.explanation: The 25 July 2018 elections were held under heavy security after years of militancy.

questions.prompt: Pakistan celebrated its 75th independence anniversary (Azadi Ka Amrit-like milestone) in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan marked 75 years of independence in August 2022.

questions.prompt: The Indus Valley Civilisation was contemporary with which ancient civilisation?
questions.explanation: It flourished alongside Egypt and Mesopotamia.

questions.prompt: The city of Harappa is located on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: Harappa lies on the old course of the Ravi River.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at the First Battle of Panipat.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the British and:
questions.explanation: Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey.

questions.prompt: The first Governor-General of British India was:
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of India.

questions.prompt: The War of Independence (1857) began at which city?
questions.explanation: The uprising broke out at Meerut in May 1857.

questions.prompt: The British abolished the East India Company's rule in which year?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1858 transferred power to the Crown.

questions.prompt: The Swadeshi Movement was launched in response to:
questions.explanation: Swadeshi arose against the 1905 partition of Bengal.

questions.prompt: The Chauri Chaura incident (1922) is associated with:
questions.explanation: The Chauri Chaura violence ended the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.prompt: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in:
questions.explanation: The massacre at Amritsar took place on 13 April 1919.

questions.prompt: Who ordered the Jallianwala Bagh firing?
questions.explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered the firing.

questions.prompt: The Round Table Conferences were held in which city?
questions.explanation: All three Round Table Conferences met in London (1930–32).

questions.prompt: The Cripps Mission came to India in:
questions.explanation: The Cripps Mission visited India in March 1942.

questions.prompt: The Hindu ruler who fought against Mahmud of Ghazni was:
questions.explanation: Raja Jaipal led resistance against Mahmud of Ghazni.

questions.prompt: The Delhi Sultanate was founded by:
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-Din Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.

questions.prompt: The Sultanate's first woman ruler was:
questions.explanation: Razia Sultana ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240.

questions.prompt: The Ghaznavid ruler who attacked Somnath temple was:
questions.explanation: Mahmud of Ghazni raided Somnath in 1025.

questions.prompt: The Taj Mahal was built by which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal for Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between Akbar and:
questions.explanation: Akbar's forces defeated Maharana Pratap at Haldighati.

questions.prompt: The Sikh Empire in Punjab was founded by:
questions.explanation: Maharaja Ranjit Singh founded the Sikh Empire in 1799.

questions.prompt: The British annexed Sindh in which year?
questions.explanation: Sindh was annexed by Charles Napier in 1843.

questions.prompt: The British defeated the Sikhs in the Second Anglo-Sikh War in:
questions.explanation: The Second Anglo-Sikh War ended with the annexation of Punjab in 1849.

questions.prompt: The famous Al-Beruni wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind' during the reign of:
questions.explanation: Al-Beruni accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni's campaigns.

questions.prompt: The city of Multan is famous for the shrine of:
questions.explanation: Shah Rukn-e-Alam's shrine is at Multan.

questions.prompt: The Gandhara civilisation is best known for:
questions.explanation: Gandhara is famed for Greco-Buddhist art.

questions.prompt: The East India Company received trading rights in India from:
questions.explanation: Jahangir granted the Company trading rights in 1608–1613.

questions.prompt: The last Mughal emperor was:
questions.explanation: Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled after 1857.

questions.prompt: The Mauryan emperor who spread Buddhism was:
questions.explanation: Ashoka promoted Buddhism across the subcontinent.

questions.prompt: The capital of the Indus Valley site Mohenjo-Daro was located in:
questions.explanation: Mohenjo-Daro is in Sindh, near Larkana.

questions.prompt: The British created the 'North-West Frontier Province' in:
questions.explanation: NWFP (now KPK) was separated from Punjab in 1901.

questions.prompt: The 'Sassanid' and 'Kushan' empires competed for control of which region?
questions.explanation: Gandhara was contested by Sassanids and Kushans.

questions.prompt: The 'Shah Jahan' period is famous for:
options: The golden age of Mughal architecture
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan's reign produced the Taj Mahal and Shahjahanabad.

questions.prompt: The 'Battle of Chausa' (1539) was fought between:
questions.explanation: Sher Shah defeated Humayun at Chausa.

questions.prompt: The first known ruler of the Mauryan Empire was:
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire.

questions.prompt: The 'Buddhist king' Kanishka belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Kanishka was the great Kushan ruler.

questions.prompt: The 'Raja Dahir' was the ruler of which region?
questions.explanation: Raja Dahir ruled Sindh when Muhammad bin Qasim invaded.

questions.prompt: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in:
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim invaded Sindh in 711 AD.

questions.prompt: The 'Sultanate of Delhi' lasted from:
questions.explanation: The Delhi Sultanate ran from 1206 to 1526.

questions.prompt: The 'Fatehpur Sikri' was built by:
questions.explanation: Akbar founded Fatehpur Sikri in 1571.

questions.prompt: The 'Battle of Talikota' (1565) led to the fall of which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagara fell after Talikota.

questions.prompt: The 'Mughal emperor' who banned the Jizya tax was:
questions.explanation: Akbar abolished the Jizya in 1564.

questions.prompt: The 'Guru Granth Sahib' was compiled by:
questions.explanation: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth.

questions.prompt: The 'Anglo-Sikh' Treaty of 1846 was signed after which war?
questions.explanation: The treaty followed the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46).

questions.prompt: The 'Hazara' region of KPK was historically part of which kingdom?
options: The Sikh Empire before British annexation
questions.explanation: Hazara was under the Sikh Empire before 1849.

questions.prompt: The 'Red Fort' of Delhi was built by:
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort in 1648.

questions.prompt: The 'Alauddin Khalji' was famous for:
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji introduced market regulations.

questions.prompt: The 'Sikh Empire' was annexed by the British in:
questions.explanation: Punjab was annexed after the Second Anglo-Sikh War in 1849.

questions.prompt: The 'Kushan emperor' who convened the Fourth Buddhist Council was:
questions.explanation: Kanishka convened the Fourth Buddhist Council.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh?
questions.explanation: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the MAO College in 1875, the nucleus of Aligarh Muslim University.

questions.prompt: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was headed by whom?
questions.explanation: Pethick-Lawrence led the three-member Cabinet Mission of 1946.

questions.prompt: Who was the last Viceroy of India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy, overseeing the partition in 1947.

questions.prompt: The Doctrine of Lapse was associated with which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie used the Doctrine of Lapse to annex states whose rulers died without heirs.

questions.prompt: The First War of Independence (1857) is also known as?
questions.explanation: The 1857 uprising is often called the Sepoy Mutiny or the War of Independence.

questions.prompt: The ruins of the Indus Valley Civilisation were discovered in which period?
questions.explanation: Excavations at Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro in 1921-22 revealed the Indus Valley Civilisation.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the ruins of Harappa?
questions.explanation: Daya Ram Sahni supervised the first excavations at Harappa in 1921.

questions.prompt: The excavations of Mohenjo-Daro were carried out by?
questions.explanation: R.D. Banerji led the excavation of Mohenjo-Daro in 1922.

questions.prompt: Muhammad bin Qasim was sent to conquer Sindh by whom?
questions.explanation: The Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf dispatched the 17-year-old Muhammad bin Qasim in 711.

questions.prompt: The Arab conquest of Sindh took place during the reign of which Umayyad caliph?
questions.explanation: Sindh was conquered in 711 during the reign of Caliph Walid ibn Abd al-Malik.

questions.prompt: Sher Shah Suri built which famous road connecting Bengal with the North-West?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri constructed the Grand Trunk Road, later extended by the British.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Panipat of 1761 was fought between the Marathas and?
questions.explanation: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas at Panipat in 1761.

questions.prompt: The English East India Company was formed in which year?
questions.explanation: Queen Elizabeth I granted the East India Company its charter in 1600.

questions.prompt: The Regulating Act, which brought the East India Company under British parliamentary control, was passed in?
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step of British government control over the Company.

questions.prompt: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Retired British official A.O. Hume founded the Congress in 1885.

questions.prompt: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first Congress session at Bombay in 1885.

questions.prompt: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which city?
questions.explanation: The massacre occurred at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.prompt: The Civil Disobedience Movement was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement with the Salt March in 1930.

questions.prompt: The Salt March (Dandi March) of 1930 was led by whom?
questions.explanation: Gandhi marched from Sabarmati to Dandi to break the salt law in 1930.

questions.prompt: At which session of the Congress was 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) demanded?
questions.explanation: The Congress at its Lahore session in December 1929 declared Purna Swaraj as its goal.

questions.prompt: Who was known as the 'Frontier Gandhi'?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan led the Khudai Khidmatgar movement in the NWFP.

questions.prompt: The first census of Pakistan was held in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan conducted its first national census in 1951.

questions.prompt: Which city served as the capital of Pakistan before Islamabad?
questions.explanation: Karachi was the federal capital until the seat of government moved to Islamabad.

questions.prompt: Pakistan became a republic in which year?
questions.explanation: With the 1956 Constitution, Pakistan became an Islamic Republic.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Viceroy of India under the British Crown?
questions.explanation: Lord Canning became the first Viceroy after the Crown took over in 1858.

questions.prompt: The tomb of Emperor Jahangir is located in which city?
questions.explanation: Jahangir's mausoleum stands at Shahdara on the outskirts of Lahore.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought between the British and?
questions.explanation: The British defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Mir Jafar and Shah Alam II at Buxar.

questions.prompt: The Doctrine of Subsidiary Alliance was introduced by?
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley used subsidiary alliances to bring Indian states under British control.

questions.prompt: The 'Forward Bloc' within the Congress was founded by?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Forward Bloc in 1939.

questions.prompt: The book 'Causes of the Indian Revolt' was written by?
questions.explanation: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote 'Causes of the Indian Revolt' after 1857.

questions.prompt: The Wahabi movement in India was led by?
questions.explanation: Syed Ahmad Barelvi led the Wahabi movement against Sikh rule in the early 19th century.

questions.prompt: The Government of India Act of 1858 transferred the control of India from the Company to?
options: The Secretary of State for War
questions.explanation: After 1858, India was governed in the name of the British Crown.
